questions.stem: A 49-year-old male presents to the primary care clinic for a regular follow-up. His past medical history includes coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, obesity (BMI 41.2), and obstructive sleep apnea. He takes aspirin, losartan, metformin, and glipizide. He complains of a nonproductive cough for the last 3 months when he goes to bed. The patient denies fevers, sore throat, or postnasal drip. His symptoms improve when he sleeps using more pillows, but his neck does not feel comfortable that way. On physical examination, temperature is 36.7°C, blood pressure is 139/78 mm Hg, pulse rate is 71/min, and respiration rate is 16/min. Lungs are clear to auscultation without wheezing. There is no jugular venous distension or lower extremity edema. Examination is otherwise normal. Chest X-ray is normal. Chemistry panel is as follows: Sodium 141mEq/L, Potassium 4.1mEq/L, Chloride 99mEq/L, Bicarbonates 28mEq/L, Blood urea nitrogen 10mg/dL, Creatinine 1.1mg/dL, Glucose 110mg/dL, Hemoglobin A1c 6.9%, and Pro-BNP 81pg/dL. What is the next step in management?
